fundamental.headline: Solid business, but expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 8% over the last year, it keeps 18 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, it has more cash than debt.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying more than usual: its price vs sales is higher than 83% of the last 5 years. Compared with similar companies, adjusted for growth, it's priced about in line.
drivers: Sales growth is speeding up compared with six months ago.
news: No major company news in the last two weeks.
fundamental.take: Good business, but expensive right now: patience may pay; wait for a better price. This is research, not personal advice.

timing.label: Event ahead
timing.text: Results come out on 2026-11-12; wait to see them before buying, since the price can jump either way.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 18% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 8% last year; 5%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 35% (3 years ago 47%, falling) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $35 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 36% (3 years ago 43%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $3.3B, up 32% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 5%/yr over 3 years and 7%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 30% vs a 5-year range of 28–32% (median 29%): in the middle of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: in the middle of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $3.5B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($2.0B buybacks + $1.5B dividends) = 1.3% of the company's market value. Share count down 0.2% from a year ago (about flat).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $18.56, up 9% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 5 analysts raised, 2 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $12.79, up 4% in 90 days; 0 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Semiconductor Systems 77% of sales, up 27%; Applied Global Services 20% of sales, up 22%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +41% vs a year ago · $11.58 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 41% vs sales 25%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running by about 5%, yet the stock fell after 6 of them: beats are already expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 25% from a year ago and speeding up (from -2% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $30 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 61% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 28× last year's profit (higher than 80% of the last 5 years); only 18× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Nov 12; analysts expect EPS of $4.06, up 87% from a year ago. It usually moves about 7% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 9% in 90 days (5 raised, 2 cut lately): forecasts are edging up.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
